allObjections.title: Phase B implementation vacuum
allObjections.detail: CA-14-A mandates Phase B Adversarial Surface Testing as a hard gate but provides no implementation spec, no agent assignment, and no timeline. §6.10 defines what Phase B should test but not HOW to execute it, creating an unfunded mandate that blocks all GTM clearance.

allObjections.title: Atomic-write contention deadlock risk
allObjections.detail: §7.5.1 Invariant 3's CAS pattern with 3-retry limit creates a systemic deadlock risk when multiple agents (Self-Renewal, Monitor, ACE) concurrently update ProductSSOT. The 50/100/200ms backoffs are too short for distributed systems, and persistent contention becomes 'non-retryable without operator intervention' - a production showstopper.

allObjections.title: 95-bar creates impossible bootstrap
allObjections.detail: CA-13-A's ≥95 GTM bar combined with CA-14-A's Phase B requirement creates a catch-22: new products can't reach 95 without Self-Renewal fixes, but Self-Renewal can't run without a seeded ProductSSOT row (CA-14-D Invariant 2), and the seed migrations are incomplete for 4/6 VEU products.

allObjections.title: GTM Bar Increase Risks Overhead
allObjections.detail: The proposal to increase the GTM readiness bar from 75 to 95 in §7.6 could lead to significant overhead and delays in product launches. This change may require extensive additional testing and development resources, potentially slowing down the time-to-market for new products.

allObjections.title: Phase B Testing Lacks Clear Ownership
allObjections.detail: CA-14-A introduces Phase B Adversarial Surface Testing as a hard prerequisite but does not assign a clear implementation owner. This lack of clarity could lead to confusion and inefficiencies in the testing process, as responsibilities are not clearly defined.

allObjections.title: Inconsistent Naming Conventions
allObjections.detail: The naming conventions for sibling charter keys in CA-13-B are inconsistent. The proposal uses `<agent-short-name>-executor`, which may not align with existing naming conventions and could lead to confusion or misalignment with other parts of the system.

allObjections.title: Lack of clarity
allObjections.detail: The proposal under review is overly complex and lacks clear explanations of the changes being made to the FlowAI system. Specifically, the sections on GTM Readiness Report and Phase B Adversarial Surface Testing are difficult to understand without prior knowledge of the system.

allObjections.title: Insufficient testing
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide sufficient information on how the new Phase B Adversarial Surface Testing will be tested and validated to ensure it does not introduce new bugs or issues into the system.

allObjections.title: Potential for abuse
allObjections.detail: The introduction of the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY sibling pattern and the auto_write_internal authority could potentially be abused by malicious actors, and the proposal does not provide sufficient safeguards to prevent this.

allObjections.title: Complexity of CA-13-A
allObjections.detail: The proposed changes in CA-13-A introduce significant complexity. The new GTM-ready bar of 95 and the introduction of the Near-GTM band add layers of decision-making that could slow down the clearance process. The conditional clearance path for Near-GTM scores may lead to inconsistent standards across different products.

allObjections.title: Vague Implementation in CA-14-A
allObjections.detail: CA-14-A specifies Phase B Adversarial Surface Testing as a prerequisite but does not assign an implementation owner. This lack of clear ownership could lead to delays and inconsistencies in the implementation process.

allObjections.title: Overlap with Existing Mechanisms
allObjections.detail: The proposed changes in CA-14-C overlap with existing mechanisms for remediation prioritization. The Five-Layer Intelligence Framework is already in place, and adding another layer of prioritization based on §7.6 findings could lead to confusion and redundancy.

allObjections.title: GTM bar conflation risk
allObjections.detail: Raising the GTM bar to 95 in CA-13-A, while clarifying its distinction from the Self-Audit 95/95, still risks conflation in practice.  Operators might prioritize achieving the GTM score over addressing fundamental build quality issues flagged by the Self-Audit, especially given the conditional clearance path.

allObjections.title: Phase B scope creep
allObjections.detail: CA-14-A's Phase B Adversarial Surface Testing, while valuable, lacks concrete definition of scope and adversarial techniques.  Without clear boundaries, Phase B could become overly broad and resource-intensive, potentially delaying releases without proportionally increasing product quality. The 'intentional error states' are particularly vague.

allObjections.title: Invariants too strict
allObjections.detail: CA-14-B's five safety invariants, while aiming to prevent regressions, might be overly restrictive.  The 'diff-only' and 'preserve rules' invariants could prevent necessary refactoring or code cleanup, leading to technical debt accumulation and hindering long-term maintainability.  The 'preserve rules' invariant is especially concerning.

allObjections.title: LIMITATIONS disclosure burden
allObjections.detail: The mandatory verbatim LIMITATIONS disclosure in CA-14-A, while intended to ensure transparency, could become a boilerplate exercise. Operators might simply copy-paste the required text without truly understanding or addressing the underlying limitations, diminishing the disclosure's effectiveness. The length of the verbatim text is also a concern.

allObjections.title: Atomic write contention
allObjections.detail: CA-14-D's atomic-audit-write requirement, while addressing concurrency issues, introduces the risk of contention and retry loops.  The proposed exponential backoff might not be sufficient to resolve contention in high-traffic scenarios, potentially leading to delays or failures in updating the ProductSSOT. The 3-retry limit seems arbitrary.

allObjections.title: Unproven Phase B ownership
allObjections.detail: CA-14-A introduces Phase B testing without assigning implementation ownership (§15.1 Roster). This creates ambiguity in responsibility, risking gaps in adversarial testing execution. Agent #21's expanded role isn't codified in the agent charter table.

allObjections.title: Sibling executor documentation gap
allObjections.detail: CA-13-B's EXECUTOR_REGISTRY pattern leaves §15.5's sibling charter table unpopulated. Without explicit documentation of 'aggressive-crawl-conductor-executor' in the agent roster, maintenance risks emerge from undocumented authority surfaces.

allObjections.title: Atomic write retry risks
allObjections.detail: CA-14-D's atomic-audit-write retry logic (3 attempts with 50/100/200ms backoff) may fail under high concurrency, silently dropping governance entries. §7.5.1 Invariant 3 lacks fallback to queue-based writes when CAS fails.

allObjections.title: GTM bar conflates readiness layers
allObjections.detail: CA-13-A rewrites §7.6 from a demo-facing score into a hard product-go/no-go gate at ≥95, but the proposal still keeps the same score formula based on issue severities. That makes the threshold look objective while silently changing its meaning from "demo guidance" to "full market readiness" without introducing any new measurement for actual user outcomes or revenue-critical functionality.

allObjections.title: Conditional clearance weakens the bar
allObjections.detail: CA-13-A-Q2 adds a Near-GTM conditional path where 90–94 can pass §11 Step 5 with admin signoff. That creates a loophole exactly where the proposal claims to be tightening standards, and it also makes the new 95 bar non-hard in practice unless every operator consistently refuses to use the exception.

allObjections.title: Two-distinct-95 paragraph adds complexity
allObjections.detail: The new §19.0 reconciliation tries to separate Self-Audit 95/95 from GTM Readiness ≥95, but it introduces another cross-reference layer that future authors can still misread. Because both mechanisms now share the same numeric threshold and both block Step 5, the proposal risks semantic drift rather than preventing it unless the underlying terms are renamed.

allObjections.title: Phase B gate lacks ownership
allObjections.detail: CA-14-A makes Phase B mandatory for Step 5, but it does not assign a stable owner in the canonical text. Without a named agent or execution path, the requirement can become a permanent paper gate: the system can fail clearance for lack of a designated verifier even when the product itself is functional.

allObjections.title: SSOT seeding may break first-run workflows
allObjections.detail: CA-14-D requires a preexisting ProductSSOT row before any Self-Renewal or governance write, but the draft does not specify an onboarding escape hatch for new products or migrations. That means a missing seed row becomes a hard failure mode for newly created products, which is worse than the status quo where the system could at least inspect and bootstrap from runtime state.

allObjections.title: GTM bar ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The proposal changes the GTM-ready bar from 75 to 95 (§7.6), but the rationale for this change is not clearly linked to the underlying metrics or business requirements. The impact of this change on existing products and future development is not thoroughly analyzed.

allObjections.title: Phase B testing scope
allObjections.detail: CA-14-A introduces Phase B Adversarial Surface Testing as a hard prerequisite for §11 Clearance Step 5. However, the scope and implementation details of Phase B are not clearly defined, leaving uncertainty about its effectiveness and feasibility.

allObjections.title: Five-Layer Framework role
allObjections.detail: CA-14-C clarifies that the Five-Layer Intelligence Framework is for telemetry only, not remediation prioritization. However, this change may cause confusion if not properly communicated to stakeholders, and its implications on existing processes are not fully explored.

allObjections.title: Phase B owner undefined
allObjections.detail: CA-14-A §6.10 adds Phase B Adversarial Surface Testing as a mandatory §11 Step 5 prerequisite yet CA-14-A-Q3 leaves ownership assignment to future dispatch; this leaves the five-prerequisite gate in §7.6 without an executing agent, directly contradicting the claim that Phase B produces a reliable phase_b_pass boolean.

allObjections.title: Atomic CAS contention deadlock
allObjections.detail: §7.5.1 Invariant 3 requires snapshot+CAS+rollback on every product_ssot.governance_record write with only 3 retries; concurrent triggers from Agent #3 Self-Renewal and Agent #10 Monitor (both writing delta_log and governance_record entries) can exhaust retries and emit agent.product_ssot.atomic_write_contention.v1 with no documented recovery path beyond operator intervention.

allObjections.title: GTM 95 + Phase B compound gate
allObjections.detail: CA-13-A raises §7.6 GTM bar to 95 while CA-14-A simultaneously adds Phase B as a hard fifth prerequisite in the same §11 Clearance Step 5 gate; the combined requirement exceeds any threshold previously exercised in ENTRY 010's 42/100 demonstration and lacks a rollback or staged-relaxation mechanism.

adversarial.precedent: GitHub Actions and other CI/CD systems commonly gate releases on multiple required checks; when those checks are underspecified or missing owners, teams end up blocked by process rather than code. objections.detail: CA-13-A raises §7.6 GTM bar to 95 while CA-14-A simultaneously adds Phase B as a hard fifth prerequisite in the same §11 Clearance Step 5 gate; the combined requirement exceeds any threshold previously exercised in ENTRY 010's 42/100 demonstration and lacks a rollback or staged-relaxation mechanism.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: Products that currently clear at 75–80 after Phase A surface crawl will now be permanently blocked from §11 Step 5 until both ≥95 score and full interactive adversarial testing succeed, turning the Self-Renewal loop from an accelerator into a permanent stall for all but the most mature VEU products.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal simultaneously tightens the GTM bar, adds an unimplemented Phase B gate, and imposes strict atomic-write and fix-safety invariants on a 26-agent system whose Self-Renewal Executor has never been shown to sustain the new thresholds end-to-end. These changes risk converting an already intricate governance substrate into a non-terminating loop where clearance is unreachable, violating the very productivity claims made in §7 and §10.

CA-13-A-Q1.pick_text: Reject — keep ENTRY 006's ≥75 Demo-ready bar; surface the CEO directive as an operator-product GTM bar (per-product target) rather than the §7.6 canonical band threshold.
CA-13-A-Q1.rationale: Raising the canonical band to 95 without demonstrated sustained runs at that level creates an unreachable gate.

CA-13-A-Q2.pick_text: Eliminate conditional path — ≥95 is hard; below 95 → blocked; admin cannot signoff a Near-GTM as cleared.
CA-13-A-Q2.rationale: Conditional clearance undermines the CEO directive that 95 is the true GTM bar.

CA-13-A-Q3.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-A-Q3.rationale: The reconciliation paragraph is needed but must also address the new Phase B gate introduced by CA-14-A.

CA-13-B-Q1.pick_text: Defer — wait for engineering dispatch to populate the §15.5 sibling-row table with executor entries; amend §15 intro + §15.1 at that same commit (joint disposition).
CA-13-B-Q1.rationale: Text change without the actual registry rows risks further divergence between canonical and code.

CA-13-B-Q2.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-B-Q2.rationale: Naming should be decided only after the sibling executors are actually implemented and tested.

CA-14-A-Q1.pick_text: Reject — Phase A is sufficient; the four-prerequisite gate from ENTRY 006 stays; Phase B may surface as advisory signal without blocking.
CA-14-A-Q1.rationale: Phase B is valuable but cannot be made mandatory while its owner and implementation remain undefined.

CA-14-A-Q2.pick_text: Adopt no verbatim wording — require disclosure but let operator phrase.
CA-14-A-Q2.rationale: Verbatim legal-style text will be ignored or paraphrased in practice.

CA-14-A-Q3.pick_text: Defer ownership — CA-14-A canonizes the requirement; engineering dispatch picks the owner in a follow-up.
CA-14-A-Q3.rationale: Assigning ownership before the capability exists is premature.

CA-14-A-Q4.pick_text: Reject Locked Rule 19 — the §6.10 + §7.6 + §7 LIMITATIONS amendments are sufficient; no new Locked Rule needed.
CA-14-A-Q4.rationale: Adding another Locked Rule increases rigidity without adding enforcement.

CA-14-B-Q1.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-14-B-Q1.rationale: The invariants belong in both the spec and an executable test harness, not solely in canonical SSOT.

CA-14-B-Q2.pick_text: Soften to "rarely ships" — acknowledges edge cases.
CA-14-B-Q2.rationale: Absolute "NEVER" language is unrealistic given the complexity of the fix pipeline.

CA-14-B-Q3.rationale: Safety invariants touch governance, remediation, and output contract simultaneously.

CA-14-C-Q1.pick_text: Ratify with stronger language — "Five-Layer tags MUST NOT influence remediation ordering" (explicit prohibition vs. "DO NOT influence").
CA-14-C-Q1.rationale: Weak language leaves room for future implicit re-introduction of Five-Layer ordering.

CA-14-C-Q2.pick_text: Don't touch §9 — the §6.10 + §7.6 amendments are sufficient.
CA-14-C-Q2.rationale: Step 6 row edits risk format drift; the §7.6 paragraph already governs prioritization.

CA-14-D-Q1.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-14-D-Q1.rationale: The invariants are necessary but must include explicit contention-resolution SLAs and operator tooling.

CA-14-D-Q2.pick_text: Ratify CA-14 immediately; remaining 4 products seeded per operator-driven dispatch order.
CA-14-D-Q2.rationale: Blocking ratification on seeding of non-critical products stalls other safety improvements.

perReviewer.overallNotes: Multiple new mandatory gates and invariants are introduced without demonstrated end-to-end execution at the tightened thresholds.
